subtitle: Free 3D driving-school simulator – German traffic rules on the real road network
freeDesc: Drive freely through Baunatal, Kassel and the whole region around them. The instructor speaks up when you make a mistake.
freeTramDesc: Drive the tram on the tracks of Kassel and Baunatal, from the stop you choose. The instructor speaks up when you make a mistake.
freeWalkDesc: Walk through the town: on the pavement, across at the crossings, with the push buttons of the pedestrian lights – and get on a tram at its stop. The instructor speaks up when you break a rule.
freeFlyDesc: Take off from an airfield of northern Hesse in a light aeroplane and fly over the land – from Kassel Airport or one of the small fields. Throttle, stick, flaps: it flies as such an aeroplane does.
demoDesc: The car drives by itself from the start point to places you choose – watch how the way there is driven by the rules.
demoTramDesc: The tram drives by itself from the stop you chose: it keeps to the speeds, serves every stop and waits at red lights. Use the controller to take over.
examDesc: About 20 to 25 minutes following the examiner: residential streets, traffic lights, roundabout, priority, country road. Serious faults end the test.
learn.title: Learn
learn.hint: Practise the theory: a test exam, the signs, spotting dangers – and see where you stand.
learn.examDesc: 30 questions in 45 minutes, as in the theory test for class B.
learn.signsDesc: Every sign of the game: its meaning or its number. Those you miss come back sooner.
learn.dangerDesc: A frozen moment of each theory scene: why must you be ready to brake?
learn.logDesc: All lessons, tasks, scenes and results: what you have tried and passed.
learn.examRules: 30 questions – 20 of the basic material and 10 for class B – worth 2 to 5 points each, 110 in all. Some have more than one right answer: tick all of them. You fail with more than 10 error points, or with two wrong 5-point questions. You have 45 minutes.
learn.examOwn: The questions are our own, written from the road traffic regulations (StVO) and the driving-licence rules – not those of the official test.
learn.handInOpen: {n} questions are not answered yet. Hand in anyway?
learn.leaveExam: Leave the exam? It will not be counted.
learn.timeUp: Time is up – what was not answered counts as wrong.
learn.wrongFive: Two 5-point questions wrong: that alone means failing.
learn.askNumber: Which number does this sign have in the catalogue?
learn.dangerAsk: Why must you be ready to brake here?
menuStage: The vehicle large in 3D, with icons
menuMore: Show the place and the options
menuLess: Fold the place and the options away
menuCarousel: Rows of cards over the 3D picture
semi.do.uPull: Pull forward slowly – the fifth wheel comes out from under the trailer, which stays on its landing gear.
semi.do.cApproach: Reverse in line with the trailer until the fifth wheel stands just before the trailer’s front edge. Stop and apply the handbrake.
semi.do.cLatch: Reverse at a crawl under the trailer until the fifth wheel locks on the kingpin, then apply the handbrake.
semi.step.uLeg: Wind down the landing gear until its feet stand on the ground
semi.step.uOpen: Pull the fifth wheel’s release handle
semi.step.cCheck: Check the trailer: secured? Kingpin, fifth wheel open and greased
semi.step.cHeight: Compare heights: the trailer’s plate a little below the fifth wheel
semi.step.cLocked: Check: jaws closed round the kingpin, handle home, safety catch in
semi.step.cLeg: Wind up the landing gear and stow the crank
v.semiJackknife.title: Jack-knifed
v.semiJackknife.why: The semi-trailer swung round until it stood against the tractor’s cab. Reversing, the trailer turns ever further once it has started – steer back early, little at a time, and pull forward before the angle grows too large.
ctl.semiReverse: Reverse gear, then throttle gently: reversing under the trailer, to the ramp or round the corner – at walking pace, and at a crawl for the last metre under the trailer (faster is a fault)
ctl.semiHandbrake: Handbrake: on before every step on foot – the list of things to do at the trailer shows only while the lorry stands with it on
ctl.semiChoices: On foot (standing, handbrake on, during coupling and uncoupling): the things to do at the trailer – brake, chocks, landing gear, red and yellow line, cables, the fifth wheel’s handle, the checks. Tap them in the right order: one out of turn is a fault and is not done
ctl.semiBack: Close the list and go back to the driver’s seat – to drive the next step
ctl.semiMirror: Mirrors: while reversing, watch the trailer’s end in both, and its angle to the tractor
ctl.semiCamera: Camera: from high above while reversing on the yard, close by while coupling

news.1_7_0.learn: Learn: a theory exam like the real one (30 of our own questions in 45 minutes, with error points), a sign trainer, “spot the danger” and a lesson log; 16 new theory lessons (level crossings, parking signs, distance, narrowings, buses, night, fog, an accident, the lorry's blind spot, merging, tunnels, an elderly pedestrian, deer, a police officer's signals, a flagman) and the basic driving tasks of class B on the practice yard.
news.1_7_0.crossings: Level crossings work: lights, barriers and bells with the trains, beacons before them, the rules of § 19; deer and wild boar cross country roads at dusk; traffic gives way at narrowed streets.
news.1_7_0.together: Play together and keep your progress: with a server (its own program, for your own server) you sign in with a code, your lessons and favourites follow you to other devices, photos and 360° panoramas can be uploaded and viewed, and several players drive in the same world.
news.1_7_0.history: “What's new” also lists the development versions 0.1.0–0.9.0 – 0.8.0 and 0.9.0 can be played – and every version shows its size in lines of code.
news.1_7_0.streets: Baunatal centre's streets as they really are – compared by eye with street photos and the official aerial photos: the right widths and lanes, pavements only where they are, parked cars along the kerbs and in bays, cycle lanes, gutters, verges, traffic islands with keep-right signs, raised tables, give-way lines, zigzags and painted “30”s, flush driveways, paths and squares.
news.1_7_0.green: Trees, woods and hedges where they really stand, with crowns of their real size; lawns instead of grey paving, no lake where there is a meadow, smooth edges of fields and car parks, flat and green roofs where they are, and the buildings that were missing.
news.1_7_0.watch: Watch any vehicle – a car, a bus, the police, an ambulance, a tram – by tapping it, and take it over; watched vehicles turn smoothly with their wheels steering. On the show place every model can be driven.
news.1_7_0.arcade: Arcade options: driving without gears and handbrake (the pedals decide forward or back, the car holds itself), faster time while you drive yourself, and roads that grip the same in any weather. A button resets the settings.
news.1_7_0.foot: On foot: three ways to walk – classic with a stick on phones, as before, or tap where to go (across at the zebra) – and running on a switch. A short tap on the world offers “Teleport here”.
news.1_7_0.camera: The free camera really flies – W A S D, Q E up and down, the wheel sets its speed – and the world loads round it. Tapping the minimap opens the big map; the display can be arranged from the pause menu or by holding a part.
news.1_7_0.voices: Better voices: the best voice of your browser for the language, never one of another language, chosen, faster or slower, higher or lower in the settings; numbers and units are read as words.
news.1_7_0.lessons: Lessons start with a choice: where (the practice ground, anywhere in town or a district picked on a map) and whether you drive or watch – the autopilot drives it with the instructor's remarks, and you can take over.
news.1_7_0.moped: Mopeds and motorcycles no longer jump and flip on kerbs and bumps; stops stand on the pavement, not on the road.
news.1_7_0.view: Full screen with one tap (the button at the top or in the pause menu), and the whole display hidden for a clean view (the button beside it or F2).
news.1_7_0.more: Red close buttons everywhere, and many smaller fixes.
news.1_7_1.buttons: The buttons for full screen and hiding the display no longer cover the big map's search, and on touch screens they are in the ⋯ menu instead of over it.
news.1_7_1.solid: Vehicles are solid: you can no longer drive into a bus (or any car) – a hit counts anywhere along its body, not only at the front.
news.1_7_1.grip: Simpler driving by default: every road and field grips as dry asphalt in any weather (no sliding on grass or in the rain); the real road physics stay one switch away under Arcade.
news.1_7_1.nomercy: A new graphics preset “No mercy”: rain and snow on the windscreen, water on the roads, mud on the body and the real seasons – only there now (and in the advanced settings), never on by itself; every other preset is always summer.
news.1_7_2.limiter: The speed limiter no longer holds the car at a limit the road does not have: a road matched only weakly – a gap in the surface, a junction area, a road on a bridge – no longer takes the limit of the motorway under it.
news.1_7_2.drive: A tap on a place offers two buttons now: “Teleport here” as before, and “Drive there”, which sends the vehicle off by itself to the road nearest the point you tapped.
news.1_7_2.turn: Turn the vehicle round with F3 (or “Turn around” in the ⋯ menu): into the lane of the other direction where there is one, otherwise on the spot.
news.1_7_2.bridge: Driving over a bridge no longer counts as driving through water: only the water a wheel really reaches into wets the brakes, washes the car or stalls the engine – on a bridge deck high above a river nothing of the river touches the wheels.
news.1_7_2.signs: Conditional speed limits (“80 when wet”, “100 from 10 pm”) are signed now: the sign with its time plate stands where the limit begins, on every road of the map.
news.1_7_4.regions: The game is no longer tied to one map: it can load a region of its own. Regions of map-assets are listed in the settings, beside the map pack; choosing one loads its own streets, places and extent instead of this website's map. Regions arrive as the maps for them are published – a region is one map at a time, read while playing.
news.1_7_4.geo: The world's coordinates grew up: a map anywhere can name its own place, and a projection for every UTM zone is ready, so regions beyond the north-west of Germany can be built and loaded.
news.1_7_5.steer: Steering is yours to set: a slider for how sharply the keys turn, the speed limiter off by default, and a free drive that begins with the engine running and the way ready to drive.
news.1_7_5.mobile: The phone steers too: tilt it left or right to turn (a setting, off until you ask for it), and a manual gearbox can be changed there at last – a clutch pedal joins the pedals on the screen.
news.1_7_5.autopilot: While the autopilot drives by itself, the HUD offers a stop button: one tap and you take the wheel.
news.1_7_5.map: The map searches for a line of trams or buses by number ("5", "N3") and lays its whole way out; the place panel on a point of the map has a close button of its own.
news.1_7_5.windscreen: Rain on the windscreen in the "No mercy" graphics is water again: it no longer shows a ghost of the picture before it.
news.1_7_5.more: The gauge says how much fuel is left as a percentage, the "⋯" menu has a close button, and the low graphics preset keeps the resolution you chose for it.
news.1_7_6.tabs: The settings are in tabs now – Driving, Graphics, Sound & weather, Display, Map & region – so a long list of settings is no longer one wall of rows.
news.1_7_6.grass: Grass stands up out of the ground on the "No mercy" graphics: blades in a field bend in the wind that travels over it, so a meadow ripples as the wind moves across.
news.1_7_6.fixes: A field can lie flat as a road too (a setting beside "No road physics"), the fuel amount stands beside its gauge, rain on the windscreen is water again, a line numbered with one digit ("5") can be searched for, and a phone saved to steer by tilting steers from the start.
news.1_7_7.regions: More than three hundred maps to drive on: towns and lands of Belgium, Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy, Norway and ten German regions, beside the two of Hesse. The game reads the region you are in from your IP address when it first starts – no permission asked – and opens there; any of them can be chosen in the settings.
news.1_7_7.archive: Every version can be played again: the earlier ones moved to an archive site of their own, so all of them fit beside the map – even the first ones from before 1.3.0, each on the map it had then. The version picker says when a version knows only the Nordhessen map (regions came in 1.7.4).
news.1_7_7.controls: The autopilot's stop sits in the "⋯" menu now, not as a button over the picture (it was landing in the middle of a phone's screen); the pedals on the screen are smaller and square; and steering by tilting the phone reads whichever way it is turned – it was reading the wrong axis on many phones.
news.1_7_3.hesse: The game now covers all of Hesse and eight more regions of Germany – Bayern, Baden-Württemberg, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Hamburg, Bremen, Saarland, Rheinland-Pfalz and Niedersachsen – each as its own map of the site, so the simulator grows with the maps published for it without a new game version.
news.1_7_3.devmap: A developer mode for the map: with it on, a tile that has more than one version shows a label in the corner while you drive on it; tapping it lists every version – the base one, the stable patches and the test builds, with the one you are driving on marked – and asks when to load the one you pick: now, or the next time you drive into that part of the map.
news.1_7_3.baunatal: About 250 places in Baunatal centre are drawn truer to life, compared with the street panoramas and the aerial photographs.
news.1_7_3.parts: Maps arrive as parts (map-assets), read from raw.githubusercontent.com so a page on another origin can fetch them; they are decompressed as they are read – gzip, deflate, brotli or lzma2 (xz) – so they stay small, and in the developer mode a part can be picked up while playing, with a progress bar showing the per cent and the megabytes.
news.1_6_0.town: Baunatal centre as it really is: in about a square kilometre round Schubertstraße the houses have their real wall and roof colours and materials – facing brick included – and the trees stand where they really are; on medium graphics and up the measured windows, doors, balconies and plinths of the walls are drawn.
news.1_6_0.transit: Trams and buses keep their timetables: they come to the stops when the departure boards say. Tapping a tram or bus on the map opens a small menu beside it: “Show its line” and “Attach camera”.
news.1_6_0.versions: Play any version since 1.0.0: choose it in the settings or tap it in “What's new”; the notes now show the time of each release. A bigger or other map can be loaded from a file of the releases.
news.1_6_0.routes: Set routes: six routes through Baunatal, Kassel, the country and on the A 49 – leaving the route or driving it the wrong way is a fault. Lessons can take place on the practice ground, anywhere in town or in a district chosen.
news.1_6_0.spawn: A car here: on foot or in the crane, put a car beside you, on the ground you tap or at a place on the map (the area that is loaded is outlined) – tap it to get in. On request the game starts where you really are, and “Place precisely” puts you exactly at the chosen spot.
news.1_6_0.forklift: The forklift: its camera turns with the mouse and the finger and goes round side – seat – behind – free, the clicks work, you get off and on again, its free drive starts at the chosen place and “Forklift work” has the yard tasks. You can climb down from the tower crane, the mobile crane's buttons answer on phones, and heavy vehicles steer as slowly as they really do.
news.1_6_0.camera: Zoom with two fingers or the wheel (on foot and in the driver's seat), the inside mirror moves and resizes – in the car or on the display –, every part of the display can be arranged, a tap on the vehicle's screen opens the map, and “press T” blinks.
news.1_6_0.pause: A clearer pause menu: going on, a grid of what can be done, and the settings at the bottom.
news.1_6_0.faster: Faster: map pieces unpack and long routes are found about twice as fast with WebAssembly (it can be switched off).
news.1_6_0.more: Menu vehicles stand in the street, not in houses, and town signs only where they really are.
news.1_5_0.vehicles: New vehicles: an articulated lorry (CE) with its fifth wheel, landing legs and its own coupling lesson; class C is now a three-axle 26-tonne truck; and a forklift with its mast, load chart and tasks on the practice yard.
news.1_5_0.doors: The car's doors, bonnet and tailgate open on their hinges – getting in and out opens the door –, you can sit in any seat and ride along, and trailers and box bodies open at the back as they really do.
news.1_5_0.night: At night the headlights light the road; dip the main beam for oncoming traffic and when following (§ 17 StVO) – the others flash you if you dazzle them; a headlight flasher and an optional main-beam assist.
news.1_5_0.weather: On “Very high”: rain and snow on the windscreen and the wipers (8, washer 7), and real water in rivers and lakes; driving through water washes the car – and too deep, the engine stalls.
news.1_5_0.traffic: Queues get a small label with their length and wait, and the traffic gets past what blocks its way – into the other lane, over the oncoming lane when it is clear, or onto the verge.
news.1_5_0.change: Change vehicle in the pause menu, here and now, without loading again; on foot, “Follow my real position” lets you walk where you really are; the F1 page explains every key and button and when it works; town signs only where they really stand; a lighter low preset for weak phones.
news.1_5_0.watch: Watch any tram or bus from the map – also from the main menu's map –, the camera going with it, and take it over when you touch a control.
news.1_5_0.layers: On the map: police cars, ambulances and fire engines, roadworks and demonstrations – watch them like a tram –, fuel stations and car washes with their prices (today's with your own key of Tankerkönig), and a Layers panel to choose what is shown.
news.1_5_0.favourites: Favourite places: a right-click (or a long press) on the map or the ☆ in its place panel keeps a place – a star on the map, in the plan panel and in the search.
news.1_5_0.search: The big map has a search field for towns, stops, streets and addresses, and a button for your own location (the browser asks first): start there, jump there, or let the autopilot take you there.
news.1_5_0.autopilot: Tap a place on the map: “Autopilot: drive there” – or, in the aeroplane, “fly there” (it takes off first). The demonstration flight is in every menu, and an AP button is at hand while flying.
news.1_5_0.plane: Getting out of the aeroplane: on the ground beside it (and back in), in the air down to the ground below – a new aeroplane waits at the nearest runway. G no longer gets out in flight.
news.1_5_0.foot: On foot you begin at Baunatal Stadtmitte, in front of its departure board.
news.1_5_0.touch: On touch screens the camera turns the way your finger moves, as with the mouse; on foot, the pedal pressed near its top runs.
news.1_5_0.loading: The loading screens count steadily up and show how many megabytes have been downloaded.
news.1_5_0.lights: Trucks, buses, tractors and cranes switch their headlights and tail lamps with the light switch; working a crane, the lights, hazard lights and horn work too.
news.1_5_0.more: Also: looking left, right and back on foot; tapping the indicator arrows switches the hazard lights off; trailers stand straight behind the vehicle in the menu; “Turn engine off” in place of the starter while the engine runs; the crane's tip is a button on touch screens; stop shelters no longer stand on the road; people on foot walk round your car instead of through it; the camera behind the vehicle no longer twitches in and out while driving; bare trees in winter look like trees again.
news.1_4_0.menu: A new main menu: the vehicle large in 3D – swipe to change it, round icons for the kinds, one big button to start. The two menus of before are still there in the settings.
news.1_4_0.cranes: Cranes: a tower crane on a building site, a mobile crane that drives on the road and sets up its outriggers, and a loader crane on a truck – with load charts, a load moment limiter, a guided start and real lifting tasks.
news.1_4_0.theory: Theory lessons: 13 difficult situations shown in 3D – right before left, the tram, the emergency corridor, the school bus, the blind spot … – each with a question, the answer and its paragraph of the StVO.
news.1_4_0.traffic: More life on the roads: police, ambulances and fire engines with blue lights and sirens (make way, form the emergency corridor), roadworks with temporary lights, now and then a demonstration in town, and people on foot who go about their business, wait at the lights and look before they cross.
news.1_4_0.weather: Real weather where you drive (Open-Meteo): rain, snow, fog and thunderstorms, wet roads with less grip – and the seasons: snow in winter, coloured leaves in autumn, blossom in spring.
news.1_4_0.arcade: Arcade (pause menu): set the world to another day and hour, choose the season and the weather, and let time run up to 8× faster while the autopilot drives.
news.1_4_0.services: Fuel stations and car washes where they really are: fill up – every vehicle now uses fuel – and wash the dirt off the car. Trucks are loaded with pallets by forklift before they set off.
news.1_4_0.signs: Small timers over the traffic lights (tap one to switch it on), many more traffic signs – also those valid only at certain times, like 30 from 22 to 6 h – and town signs wherever a road enters a town.
news.1_4_0.plane: The aeroplane flies by itself (T): take-off, circuit and landing, holding height and heading, or to a place on the map. Flying by hand is helped (no stall, wings level when let go), and on the map you choose the height to start in the air.
news.1_4_0.maps: Maps: aerial photos from the start; drag the corner map to look around; draw the way the autopilot is to drive; every tram and bus on the map in its line's colour – tap it to watch it or take it over –; stops with their next departures; the places and ways looked for before.
news.1_4_0.transit: Buses run to their real timetables too, and departure boards at the stops show trams and buses. The trams' doors open and close, and you can get out of the tram and walk on.
news.1_4_0.cockpit: In the driver's seat the live map is on the vehicle's own screen; on “Very high” the car is much finer, outside and in; Y zooms into a mirror – for parking in a garage.
news.1_4_0.sounds: Every vehicle sounds like itself – engines, tram motors, the aeroplane's propeller, air brakes and doors – and there is music made as it plays (off unless you switch it on).
news.1_4_0.autopilot: The autopilot lets you take the wheel for a moment and drives on to its places when you let go, and it no longer stays stuck behind an obstacle.
news.1_4_0.more: Also: walk as far as you like from your vehicle; hit a wall at 70 km/h or more and the vehicle goes up in flames – take a new one; the motorcyclist looks into the bends; smaller controls on phones; the first loading shows its percentage; the camera goes much further back; D comes before R; the handbrake lamp is clearer; no more signs standing on the road.
news.1_3_0.menu: A new main menu: rows of cards over the 3D picture – the vehicle, the town and the place, the options, how to start – with the vehicle you chose standing where the drive begins. The simple list is still there in the settings.
news.1_3_0.replay: Replays: watch a drive again 1:1 from the pause menu or the result – behind the vehicle, from the driver's seat or freely round it, slower or faster, with the instructor's notes on the timeline.
news.1_3_0.timetables: The trams run to their real timetables, the departure boards show the real departures, and your own tram is on time or late.
news.1_3_0.busLines: City buses run their real lines, with number and destination on the front.
news.1_3_0.pantograph: The tram takes its power from the wire: raise the pantograph before it pulls (P), and lower it where the wire ends.
news.1_3_0.coupled: Two trams coupled together, or one with a trailer car – to drive yourself, and in the traffic.
news.1_3_0.figure: On foot you can see yourself: the camera key shows you from behind.
news.1_3_0.models: Every model: a test place with every vehicle, the trams, the aeroplane and the traffic of the game side by side.
news.1_2_0.plane: Fly: a light aeroplane takes off from the airfields of northern Hesse – Kassel Airport and the small fields – with flight physics of its own, a cockpit with all its instruments, and the runways drawn on the ground.
news.1_2_0.onFoot: On foot: walk and run (as fast as the settings say) anywhere, press the button at a pedestrian light, cross at zebra crossings where the cars stop for you – and ride trams and buses as a passenger.
news.1_2_0.stops: Stops you can see: platforms, shelters, stop signs with their names, departure boards and people who wait, get on and get off; the overhead line and the tram signals.
news.1_2_0.tramLines: Trams run their real lines, the number and destination on the front. The tram starts at a stop you choose, drives by itself on a demonstration drive, and the map shows the tracks and the stops.
news.1_2_0.busLine: City buses in the traffic, and a lesson for the bus: five stops with doors, passengers and pulling out.
news.1_2_0.powers: Every vehicle has engine powers of its own to choose from, within what its licence class allows.
news.1_2_0.motorcycle: New motorcycles: a model of its own for each class, with a rider who holds the handlebar.
news.1_2_0.farView: The far view: the hills on the horizon, and the land below an aeroplane.
news.1_2_0.tours: Tours: say what a tour is to avoid and to look for, watch it being planned, and find the tours you drove with their dates.
news.1_2_0.loading: Loading shows how far it is.
news.1_2_0.fixes: Fixed: after a jump on the map the tram is put back on its tracks properly and can be driven.
news.1_2_0.carModel: Fixed: the car (class B) started as a motorcycle – now it is a car again.
news.1_1_0.tram: Drive a tram on the tracks of Kassel and Baunatal: power and brake with one controller, the way at a switch with the indicator, the doors at the stops – passengers get off and on. With a lesson of five stops.
news.1_1_0.classes: Every German licence class now has its vehicle: also moped (AM), 125 (A1), motorcycle up to 35 kW (A2), truck 7.5 t (C1) with trailer (C1E), minibus (D1) with trailer (D1E), bus with trailer (DE) and the 40 km/h tractor (L); the tractor of class T now runs 60 km/h.
news.1_1_0.graphics: Graphics settings: presets that leave the resolutions alone, the size of the interface, the display and 3D resolution apart – and advanced settings for shadows, view distance, trees and plain buildings without windows.
news.1_1_0.screen: In the driver's seat of the car the map can be shown on its own screen (settings).
news.1_1_0.wheels: Fixed: the tractor, the trucks and the bus no longer float above the road – their wheels stand on it.
news.1_1_0.onFoot: On foot, the reminder of the driving keys and the speed strip are no longer shown.
news.1_0_0.intro: The first release. This version of the game includes at least:
news.1_0_0.map: Northern Hesse as it really is: the city of Kassel and five districts – 6,900 km², 115 towns and municipalities, every road and track, a million buildings in their real shape, the terrain from the official elevation model.
news.1_0_0.rules: Signs, traffic lights, zebra crossings, speed limits, one-way streets and turn bans where they really are – and where the map says nothing, the German rules apply.
news.1_0_0.instructor: An instructor in the passenger seat: the rules of the road are watched, every fault is explained with its paragraph of the StVO, counted in points and kept in the log of faults, linked to the official text. On request the speed limit and the right of way at the next junction are shown.
news.1_0_0.lessons: Lessons from the first start to the motorway – right before left, priority signs, traffic lights, roundabouts, country roads – and a test drive with its result.
news.1_0_0.vehicles: A vehicle for every licence class: car (B), car with trailer (BE), motorcycle (A), truck (C), truck with trailer (CE, with the coupling and the manoeuvres of the test), bus (D) and tractor (T) – each with its own speed limits.
news.1_0_0.physics: Driving as in a real vehicle: suspension, tyres, an engine with clutch, stalling and starter – manual gearbox, clutch help or automatic, the engine power to choose.
news.1_0_0.traffic: Traffic that keeps to the rules, pedestrians at the crossings, cyclists on the cycle tracks – look over your shoulder before turning right – and trams and trains on the real tracks.
news.1_0_0.lights: Traffic lights with a green arrow for turning right, and lights that are out of order: flashing amber, the signs apply.
news.1_0_0.plan: Plan a drive: choose destinations on the map or by address – the car drives there by itself and says what it is doing, or you drive and are guided.
news.1_0_0.voice: Directions on the screen and spoken, with the lane to get into before a junction.
news.1_0_0.tours: Tours through the streets: choose how many kilometres, and the route takes in as many different streets as possible.
news.1_0_0.onFoot: On foot: get out, walk round the vehicle and check the tyres and lights, open the door and get in. A drive can also begin beside the vehicle.
news.1_0_0.views: Three views – the driver's seat with working mirrors, behind the vehicle, a free camera –, a big map with aerial photos, and real street photos of the place where you are.
news.1_0_0.start: Start at one of 400 places in 115 towns or at any address – or jump there from the pause menu or the big map.
news.1_0_0.controls: Keyboard, gamepad, steering wheel with pedals and gear stick, or the touch screen of a phone. Settings, faults and the route driven are kept in the browser.
news.1_0_0.settings: Settings for graphics, mirrors, traffic, sound, the gearbox, the camera and more – the frames per second can be shown.
news.1_0_0.languages: 28 languages, every one complete – among them all languages in which the theory test can be taken in Germany.
news.1_0_0.free: Free software (AGPL-3.0), made from open data only: it runs in the browser, nothing to install.
news.devIntro: The steps on the way to 1.0.0, made on 15 and 16 November 2026. From 0.8.0 on they can be played on today's map; the earlier ones read a map of another form and are listed only.

news.0_9_0.driver: The automatic driver stops at a light or a stop sign at the very end of its way, and no longer cuts sharp bends into the lane of oncoming cars.
news.0_9_0.plan: The plan panel of the big map on low screens: the buttons that start a drive stay in view in one row at its foot.
news.0_8_0.camera: A free camera (V switches outside – cockpit – free): turn it by dragging or with a finger, move it with the right mouse button, two fingers or Alt + W A S D, come nearer with the wheel or a pinch. It stays where it is put while the car drives on.
news.0_8_0.tours: Tours of the streets: choose a length in kilometres, and a way through as many different streets as possible is planned – back to the start or on to a destination. Drive it or let the car drive it.
news.0_8_0.plan: “Plan a drive” on the big map: destinations by a tap or by address, anywhere on the map – the car drives there by itself, or you drive and are shown the way.
news.0_8_0.map: A much bigger map: the city of Kassel, Baunatal and most of the district of Kassel, 1,087 km² – loaded in pieces around the car, so that a region of any size can be played.
news.0_8_0.lanes: Nothing stands in a lane any more: posts, lamps, trees, walls and corners of houses in the way are moved or left out. “Back on the road” puts the car where it touches nothing.
news.0_8_0.driver: The automatic driver slows down in time for bends further ahead, stays behind the line at a red light, and is no longer judged to turn where it went straight on.
news.0_8_0.phone: On a phone the buttons of the big map no longer overlap, and the coupling steps of the truck have a button and a sheet of their own.
news.0_7_0.kassel: Baunatal and Kassel: 18 × 18 km, 2,200 km of roads, 150,000 buildings and 50,000 house numbers.
news.0_7_0.trams: Trams and trains on the real tracks: they stop at the stops and brake for each other and for cars – and road traffic brakes for them.
news.0_7_0.truck: A truck with trailer for class CE (12 t, with a 15.5 t trailer that follows the coupling and pushes back when reversing), the truck rules, and the manoeuvres of the test: coupling and uncoupling step by step, reversing round a corner and to a ramp.
news.0_7_0.demo: Demonstration drives: choose a destination on the map or by address, and the car drives there by itself, by the rules, saying what it does and why. Steering or braking hands it back to you.
news.0_7_0.bigmap: A full-screen map (M): where you are, the way driven, place names, putting the car anywhere in a free drive – optionally over the official aerial photographs of Hesse.
news.0_7_0.camera: The view from behind the car and the automatic gearbox are the defaults; the camera circles the car with the mouse, the wheel zooms, U looks back.
news.0_7_0.driving: The engine power to choose (75 PS by default), a speed limiter for keyboard and touch, calmer keyboard steering at speed, and warning lamps for the handbrake and the seat belt.
news.0_7_0.cockpit: A new cockpit with a lower dashboard and slim pillars, which can be made see-through – and graphics settings that make a visible difference: shadows, render scale, view range.
news.0_7_0.log: A log of the faults of all drives, each linked to the official text of its paragraph; settings, the start point and the way driven are kept in the browser.
news.0_7_0.more: The reality view gives coordinates to copy and more links (Google Maps, Google Earth); the instructor judges cutting in and turning left in front of oncoming traffic more fairly.
news.0_6_0.languages: 28 languages, everything translated: menus, lessons, the instructor's notices and the controls. The language follows the browser and can be changed in the menu and in the settings.
news.0_6_0.script: Arabic, Persian and Urdu are laid out from right to left. Keys are named as they are on your keyboard (QWERTZ, AZERTY …) or, on a touch screen, by their on-screen button; distances and dates are written in the form of your language.
news.0_6_0.fallback: If the browser lacks WebGL 2 or the start fails, the page says so in your language.
news.0_5_0.touch: Playable without a keyboard: new on-screen controls – steering and indicators on the left, pedals, gears and handbrake on the right, everything else behind “⋯” – that leave the middle of the picture free. They show when the screen is touched and hide when a key is pressed.
news.0_5_0.taps: A tap on the minimap opens the reality view, a tap on the street-name block the pause menu; a swipe across the picture looks over the shoulder; tips become buttons.
news.0_5_0.address: Start at an address: about 8,500 house numbers in 530 streets, found by street, number and town even when misspelt – the car is put in the right-hand lane in front of the house. In a free drive also from the pause menu.
news.0_5_0.notices: Faults (red) and hints (yellow) are shown in the street-name block, the gravest first; an announced turn stays readable below.
news.0_5_0.keys: With a keyboard, a short reminder of the keys shows while the car stands.
news.0_4_0.reality: Reality view (F or the pause menu): real street photos of the place where the car is – from Panoramax, KartaView and Mapillary, asked only when you tick them, with author, date, licence and a link to the original.
news.0_4_0.own: Your own photos and 360° panoramas: chosen as files or a folder, or dropped on the window, and placed by their GPS data, a list or the file name – read on your device, never uploaded. A panorama is shown all round and first looks the way the car faces.
news.0_4_0.links: Links that open the same place in Panoramax, Mapillary, KartaView, Google Street View and OpenStreetMap.
news.0_3_0.brakes: A lightly pressed brake now stops the car and holds it on any slope (it used to creep on over stop lines). A car on its roof or side rests there instead of sinking into the ground, and is put back on the road.
news.0_3_0.rules: Fairer judging: stopping beyond the line at red is a stop-line fault – running the red light only if you carry on into the junction; amber is judged by whether a normal stop was still possible; waiting at a line no longer counts as being in the oncoming lane.
news.0_3_0.lanes: Directions say which lane to get into before a junction; destinations are never on roads that only lead out of the map, and routes avoid turning round.
news.0_3_0.mirrors: The door mirrors sit at the front corners of the side windows: the left one is in view, and the minimap no longer covers it.
news.0_2_0.signs: More plates under the signs: direction arrows and the distance a sign applies for.
news.0_2_0.icon: The game has its own icon in the browser tab.
news.0_1_0.intro: The first version on the web: a driving-school simulator for the town of Baunatal. It had:
news.0_1_0.map: Baunatal as it really is: every street of the town and its districts, the A 49 and A 44, the roundabouts and the VW plant from OpenStreetMap; the terrain from the official 1 m elevation model and about 26,000 buildings with their real heights and roofs.
news.0_1_0.rules: Traffic lights, zebra crossings, stop and give-way signs, speed limits, 30 zones, traffic-calmed areas, one-way streets and turn bans where they really are – where the map says nothing, the German rules apply.
news.0_1_0.car: One car, driven like a real one: suspension, tyres, an engine with clutch, biting point, stalling and starter, a six-speed manual gearbox, ABS, handbrake and hill starts – or clutch help, or an automatic.
news.0_1_0.cockpit: A cockpit with steering wheel, gear stick, pedals and instruments, and three working mirrors; a look over the shoulder with the mouse or a key; views from the driver's seat and from outside.
news.0_1_0.instructor: An instructor in the passenger seat: speeding, red lights, stop signs, right of way (signs, right before left, roundabouts), indicating, zebra crossings, the wrong side, the pavement and distance are watched – each fault explained with its paragraph of the StVO.
news.0_1_0.lessons: Lessons – moving off, changing gear and stopping, right before left, priority signs, traffic lights, roundabouts, country roads, the motorway – and a test drive with its result; directions to each destination.
news.0_1_0.traffic: Traffic that keeps to lights, right of way and distance, and pedestrians at the crossings.
news.0_1_0.controls: Keyboard, gamepad, a steering wheel with pedals and gear stick, or a touch screen; sounds made by the game itself; German and English.
news.0_1_0.free: Free software (AGPL-3.0), made from open data only: it runs in the browser – nothing to install, no account.

v.forkliftTipped.title: The forklift tipped over
v.forkliftTipped.why: Too much load, too high, braked or turned too hard: the forklift went over. Drive with the load low and tilted back, slowly round turns, and never lift more than the load chart allows. If it tips: stay in the seat, hold on, lean away from the fall.
v.forkliftOverload.title: Overloaded: {kg} kg lifted, {max} kg allowed
v.forkliftOverload.why: What a forklift may lift depends on how far out the load's centre is – the load chart on the forklift says it. Check the weight before lifting; a load over the capacity lifts the rear wheels.
v.forkliftForksIn.title: Lifted with the forks only {p} % in
v.forkliftForksIn.why: A pallet lifted on the tips of the forks can tip off, and its load centre lies further out. Slide the forks in fully, up to the backrest, before lifting.
v.forkliftRearLift.title: The rear wheels lifted
v.forkliftRearLift.why: The load moment was greater than the counterweight could hold – too heavy, too far out, too high while braking. The forklift was about to tip forwards.
v.forkliftTurnFast.title: Too fast round the turn ({kmh} km/h)
v.forkliftTurnFast.why: A forklift stands on three points and is steered at the rear: in a tight turn it tips sideways easily – even more with the load raised. Slow down before turning.
v.forkliftHit.title: Ran into something at {kmh} km/h
v.forkliftHit.why: Racks, trucks and loads are not buffers: a knocked rack upright can bring the whole rack down. Approach slowly and watch the forks' tips.
v.forkliftLoadHigh.title: Driving with the load raised ({cm} cm)
v.forkliftLoadHigh.why: With the load high the forklift tips easily and the driver cannot see. Drive with the load just clear of the ground (10–20 cm); lift and lower only standing still at the place.
v.forkliftTiltForward.title: Driving with the mast tilted forwards
v.forkliftTiltForward.why: With a load on the forks the mast is tilted back while driving, so the load leans against the backrest and cannot slide off.
v.forkliftForksHigh.title: Driving with the forks raised
v.forkliftForksHigh.why: Empty, too, the forks are lowered while driving: raised forks are a danger to people and get caught on things.

v.craneOverload.title: Crane overloaded: the limiter cut off at {p} %
v.craneOverload.why: What a crane may lift depends on the radius, the boom and the outriggers – its load chart says how much. Check the load and the radius before lifting: the limiter is a safety device, not a working aid.
v.craneLoadHit.title: The load hit something ({v} m/s)
v.craneLoadHit.why: A load that strikes the building, the scaffolding or another load can tear its slings or fall. Lift it high enough, and move it slowly where it is tight.
v.craneHookHit.title: The hook block hit something
v.craneHookHit.why: Even without a load the heavy hook block can damage what it strikes or hurt somebody: move it slowly near the building and the loads.
v.craneHardLanding.title: Load set down too hard ({v} m/s)
v.craneHardLanding.why: Lower gently over the last half metre – near the ground the crane creeps. A load put down hard can break or tip over.
v.craneSwing.title: The load swung far ({m} m)
v.craneSwing.why: A swinging load is hard to stop and endangers people and the building. Start and stop every movement gently, and let a swing settle before setting the load down.
v.craneWind.title: Lifting in too strong a wind ({v} m/s, limit {max})
v.craneWind.why: Above the wind the crane is made for, the load becomes a sail: the crane can be overloaded or tip. Set the load down and stop work.
v.craneDiagonalPull.title: Load lifted at an angle ({m} m off)
v.craneDiagonalPull.why: The hook must hang straight above the middle of the load before it is lifted: pulled at an angle the load is dragged, and swings off as it comes clear.
v.craneNotLevel.title: Crane not level ({d}°)
v.craneNotLevel.why: A crane must stand as level as its maker asks – a mobile crane within 1° – or its load chart no longer holds and it can tip. Level it with the jacks before work.
v.craneTipped.title: The crane tipped over
v.craneTipped.why: The load and the boom reached beyond what the carrier, the counterweight and the outriggers could hold. Work only within the load chart, on outriggers, and within the wind limit.

v.worksLane.title: Drove into the closed lane of the roadworks
v.worksLane.why: Barriers and beacons close that lane: keep out of it and pass on the open side.
v.worksYield.title: Did not let the oncoming traffic through at the roadworks
v.worksYield.why: Sign 208: whoever has the narrowing on their side lets the oncoming traffic go first and waits before it until the way is clear.
v.narrowYield.title: Did not give way at a narrowing
v.narrowYield.why: § 6 StVO: where a kerb build-out narrows the road on your side, the oncoming traffic goes first – wait before it until the gap is clear.
v.levelCrossingRed.title: Drove over the level crossing on red
v.levelCrossingRed.why: Red lights at a level crossing – steady or flashing – mean: wait before the St Andrew's cross, a train is coming.
v.levelCrossingYellow.title: Drove over the level crossing on yellow
v.levelCrossingYellow.why: Yellow at a level crossing means: wait before the St Andrew's cross. Drive on only if you can no longer stop safely.
v.levelCrossingBarrier.title: Drove onto the crossing with the barriers coming down
v.levelCrossingBarrier.why: When the barriers are lowering or closed, wait before the St Andrew's cross – never drive under or round them.
v.levelCrossingTrain.title: Crossed the tracks in front of a train
v.levelCrossingTrain.why: Trains have the right of way at a level crossing. When one is approaching, wait before the St Andrew's cross.
v.levelCrossingStop.title: Stopped on the tracks
v.levelCrossingStop.why: Never stop on a level crossing. If there is no room behind the tracks, wait before the St Andrew's cross until there is.
v.levelCrossingOvertake.title: Overtook before a level crossing
v.levelCrossingOvertake.why: From the warning sign or the first beacon up to the tracks you must not overtake motor vehicles.
v.levelCrossingSpeed.title: Too fast over the level crossing: {speed} km/h
v.levelCrossingSpeed.why: Approach a level crossing only at a moderate speed – here at most about {limit} km/h – so that you can still stop for a train.
theory.levelCrossing.title: Level crossing
theory.levelCrossing.intro: A railway line crosses the road. The level crossing has lights beneath the St Andrew's cross, and a train is on its way.
theory.levelCrossing.1.text: As you approach, the lights at the level crossing turn yellow.
theory.levelCrossing.1.stop: Brake and stop at the line before the St Andrew's cross
theory.levelCrossing.1.go: Speed up and cross before the light turns red
theory.levelCrossing.1.slow: Cross slowly, watching out for the train
theory.levelCrossing.1.why: Yellow or red lights at a level crossing mean: wait before the St Andrew's cross. You can still stop safely here – so you must.
theory.levelCrossing.2.text: The train has passed. The lights are still red.
theory.levelCrossing.2.wait: No – I wait until the lights are out
theory.levelCrossing.2.why: Wait for as long as the lights show red: a second train may be coming. Cross only once they are out and any barriers are up.
theory.levelCrossingQueue.title: Queue at the level crossing
theory.levelCrossingQueue.intro: Behind the level crossing the traffic has come to a standstill. The car ahead of you has just crossed the tracks.
theory.levelCrossingQueue.1.text: The queue behind the tracks is not moving. There is no room for your car behind the blue one.
theory.levelCrossingQueue.1.wait: Stop before the St Andrew's cross until there is room behind the tracks
theory.levelCrossingQueue.1.close: Drive on and close up to the blue car
theory.levelCrossingQueue.1.tracks: Stop on the crossing – the lights are off
theory.levelCrossingQueue.1.why: If you cannot cross without stopping, wait before the St Andrew's cross. Never stop on the tracks: a train cannot swerve and needs hundreds of metres to stop.
theory.levelCrossingQueue.2.text: The lights are out again and the queue starts to move.
theory.levelCrossingQueue.2.ask: When do you cross the tracks?
theory.levelCrossingQueue.2.room: Once there is room for my whole car behind the tracks
theory.levelCrossingQueue.2.now: At once – the car ahead is moving
theory.levelCrossingQueue.2.why: Cross only when you can get all the way over without stopping: room for the whole car behind the tracks, not just a gap that may close again.

v.noLights.title: Drove without lights in the dark

lesson.basics.title: 1 · Pulling away, changing gear, stopping
lesson.basics.intro: Seat and mirrors are set: fasten your belt ([[KeyB]]), press the clutch and start the engine (hold [[Enter]]), select 1st gear, release the handbrake ([[Space]]). Let the clutch up slowly and add a little throttle. Change up at about 2000–2500 rpm.
lesson.rbl.title: 2 · Right before left (30 km/h zone)
lesson.rbl.intro: In residential areas without priority signs, whoever comes from the right goes first (§ 8 StVO). Approach every junction ready to stop and look right first. The 30 km/h zone lasts until the end-of-zone sign.
lesson.priority.title: 3 · Give way and stop
lesson.priority.intro: The inverted triangle (sign 205) means give way. The octagon (sign 206): stop at the line – always. The yellow diamond (sign 306) tells you that you are on the priority road.
lesson.signals.title: 4 · Traffic lights and turning
lesson.signals.intro: Amber means stop if you safely can. Turning left on green: let oncoming traffic pass. Turning right: shoulder check to the right, cyclists and pedestrians go first. Do not forget to indicate.
lesson.roundabout.title: 5 · Roundabout
lesson.roundabout.intro: At a roundabout (sign 215 with 205) traffic on the roundabout has priority. Do not indicate when entering; indicate right when leaving. Watch for pedestrians at the crossings.
lesson.rural.title: 6 · Country roads
lesson.rural.intro: Beyond the end-of-town sign the limit is 100 km/h unless signed otherwise; at the yellow town sign it is 50 km/h again. Distance: half your speed in metres. Adjust your speed early for bends and crests.
lesson.motorway.title: 7 · Motorway A 49
lesson.motorway.intro: Accelerate briskly on the slip road, mirrors, shoulder check, indicate – through traffic has priority. Keep right, overtake on the left. Recommended speed 130 km/h. Exit: indicate early, brake only on the deceleration lane.
lesson.exam.title: Driving test
lesson.exam.intro: The examiner gives the directions. Observation, speed, right of way, turning and vehicle handling are assessed. A dangerous situation or several serious faults mean a fail.
theory.title: Theory lessons
theory.desc: Difficult situations on the road, shown in 3D: watch, answer, learn why – with the paragraph of the StVO.
theory.listText: Pick a situation. The scene stops at the key moment and asks you – tap a vehicle or an answer.
theory.help: Drag to turn the view, pinch or scroll to zoom. Tap a vehicle or an answer.
theory.rbl.title: Right before left
theory.rbl.intro: A crossroads without signs or lights. Three cars arrive at the same time.
theory.rbl.1.text: No signs, no lights: three cars meet.
theory.rbl.1.why: Right before left: the blue car comes from your right, and nobody comes from its right – it goes first.
theory.rbl.2.ask: Who goes next – you or the white car?
theory.rbl.2.why: You do: the white car comes from your left, so it waits for you.
theory.bend.title: The priority road bends
theory.bend.intro: You drive on the priority road. The small sign under the yellow diamond shows its course: it bends to the left.
theory.bend.1.text: You follow the priority road round to the left.
theory.bend.1.none: No – I stay on the priority road
theory.bend.1.why: Whoever follows a priority road that bends indicates – everybody must see where you go.
theory.bend.2.text: The red car waits at the give-way sign of the side road.
theory.bend.2.why: You stay on the priority road, so you go first – even though you turn. The red car waits.
theory.leftTurn.title: Turning left on green
theory.leftTurn.intro: Green for you and for the oncoming traffic. You want to turn left.
theory.leftTurn.1.text: You wait in the junction. A car comes towards you.
theory.leftTurn.1.why: Turning left, let oncoming traffic pass first – even when you both have green.
theory.leftTurn.2.text: Somebody crosses the road you turn into, on their green.
theory.leftTurn.2.why: When you turn, people on foot go first: take special care, and wait if you must.
theory.zebra.title: Zebra crossing
theory.zebra.intro: A zebra crossing in town. Somebody walks towards it.
theory.zebra.1.text: The person is heading for the zebra crossing.
theory.zebra.1.brake: Slow down and stop – they cross first
theory.zebra.1.go: Drive on – they are not on the road yet
theory.zebra.1.horn: Sound the horn and drive on
theory.zebra.1.why: Anyone who clearly wants to use a zebra crossing must be let across: approach slowly, and stop if needed.
theory.zebra.2.text: The first person is in the other half of the road. Somebody else is coming.
theory.zebra.2.wait: No – I wait until nobody wants to cross
theory.zebra.2.why: Everybody who wants to cross may do so. Drive on only when the crossing is free and nobody is about to step onto it.
theory.tram.title: Tram at the junction
theory.tram.intro: Tram tracks run in the middle of the road. You want to turn left, and a tram comes from behind.
theory.tram.1.text: You wait to turn left. The tram beside you goes straight on.
theory.tram.1.why: When you turn, trams going your way go first – also when they come from behind. Wait beside the tracks, not on them.
theory.corridor.title: Emergency corridor
theory.corridor.intro: A road with two lanes each way, outside town. The traffic slows down to a stop.
theory.corridor.1.text: The traffic is down to walking pace. You are in the left lane.
theory.corridor.1.stay: I stay in the middle of my lane
theory.corridor.1.why: As soon as traffic moves at walking pace or stands, make a corridor: the left lane moves to the far left, all other lanes to the right.
theory.corridor.2.why: Keep the corridor open until the traffic flows again – more vehicles may come. Nobody else may drive in it.
theory.schoolBus.title: School bus at the stop
theory.schoolBus.intro: A school bus with its hazard lights on drives to its stop. You are behind it.
theory.schoolBus.1.text: The bus ahead has switched on its hazard lights and is about to stop.
theory.schoolBus.1.why: A bus driving to a stop with its hazard lights on must not be overtaken.
theory.schoolBus.2.text: The bus stands at the stop with its hazard lights on. Children get off.
theory.schoolBus.2.walk: At walking pace, with room to the bus
theory.schoolBus.2.why: Pass only at walking pace and so far away that nobody is in danger – oncoming traffic too. Children may step out: stop if you must.
theory.overtake.title: Overtaking a cyclist
theory.overtake.intro: In town, a cyclist rides ahead of you.
theory.overtake.1.text: A car is coming towards you.
theory.overtake.1.ask: Do you overtake the cyclist now?
theory.overtake.1.why: Overtake only with enough room to the side and without danger to oncoming traffic. Here there is not enough room – stay behind.
theory.overtake.2.ask: In town: how much room must you leave beside the cyclist at least?
theory.overtake.2.why: At least 1.5 m in town, at least 2 m outside town.
theory.blindSpot.title: The blind spot
theory.blindSpot.intro: You want to turn right. A cycle lane runs beside your lane.
theory.blindSpot.1.text: A cyclist rides up beside you from behind – in your blind spot (orange).
theory.blindSpot.1.why: Cyclists riding straight on go first, also when they come from behind. Look over your right shoulder before you turn.
theory.zip.title: A lane ends: the zip
theory.zip.intro: Dense traffic, and your lane ends ahead.
theory.zip.1.text: The right lane ends ahead. The left lane is full and slow.
theory.zip.1.end: Where my lane ends, taking turns
theory.zip.1.stop: I stop and wait for a big gap
theory.zip.1.why: Drive on to where your lane ends. There the cars take turns: one from the lane that goes on, one from the lane that ends.
theory.motorway.title: Joining the motorway
theory.motorway.intro: You drive onto the motorway. A lorry comes along the right lane.
theory.motorway.1.text: You are on the acceleration lane, the lorry is beside you.
theory.motorway.1.why: Traffic on the motorway goes first. Match its speed on the acceleration lane and merge into a gap – here behind the lorry.
theory.roundabout.title: Roundabout
theory.roundabout.intro: A roundabout with the signs for a roundabout and for giving way. You take the second exit.
theory.roundabout.1.text: A red car comes round the roundabout.
theory.roundabout.1.why: Traffic on the roundabout has the right of way.
theory.roundabout.2.text: The way is clear. You drive onto the roundabout.
theory.roundabout.2.ask: Do you indicate as you enter?
theory.roundabout.2.why: Entering a roundabout you do not indicate.
theory.roundabout.3.why: Indicate right before you leave the roundabout.
theory.greenArrow.title: Green arrow at red
theory.greenArrow.intro: Your light is red. Beside it there is a sign with a green arrow pointing right.
theory.greenArrow.1.text: Red light – with the green arrow sign beside it.
theory.greenArrow.1.ask: What does the green arrow allow?
theory.greenArrow.1.stop: Turning right – after stopping at the line
theory.greenArrow.1.nothing: Nothing – it is just a sign
theory.greenArrow.1.why: With the green arrow you may turn right on red – but only after stopping, and without hindering or endangering anybody.
theory.greenArrow.2.text: You have stopped. Somebody crosses in front of you on their green.
theory.greenArrow.2.why: Everybody who has green goes first – on foot or on wheels. With the green arrow, you are the one who waits.
theory.parkingSigns.title: Stopping and parking
theory.parkingSigns.intro: In town, your passenger beside you. Two signs along the kerb: first the red cross, then the single red stripe.
theory.parkingSigns.1.text: You drive under Zeichen 283 – the red cross on blue. Your passenger wants to get out.
theory.parkingSigns.1.ask: May you stop here for a moment to let her out?
theory.parkingSigns.1.why: Zeichen 283 forbids any stopping on the carriageway – not even for a moment to let somebody out. It holds from the sign to the next junction or the next sign.
theory.parkingSigns.2.text: You have stopped at the kerb under Zeichen 286 – the single red stripe.
theory.parkingSigns.2.ask: May your passenger get out here?
theory.parkingSigns.2.out: Yes – stopping to let somebody out is allowed
theory.parkingSigns.2.park: Yes – and you may leave the car here for an hour
theory.parkingSigns.2.why: Under Zeichen 286 you may stop for up to three minutes – longer only to let people in or out or to load and unload. Leaving the car, or standing longer than three minutes, is parking: not allowed here.
theory.parkingSigns.3.text: Beyond the crossroads there are no signs. You want to park there.
theory.parkingSigns.3.ask: How far from the crossroads must you stay at least?
theory.parkingSigns.3.why: No parking within 5 m of a crossroads or a junction, counted from where the edges of the carriageways meet – before it 8 m where a cycle track runs on the right. Those crossing and turning must see each other.
theory.followingDistance.title: Keeping your distance
theory.followingDistance.intro: A country road, 60 km/h. A red car drives ahead of you.
theory.followingDistance.1.text: You follow the red car at 60 km/h.
theory.followingDistance.1.ask: How much distance do you keep at least?
theory.followingDistance.1.why: Outside town the rule of thumb is half the speedometer in metres: 30 m at 60 km/h, about two seconds. The law asks for room enough to stop even when the car ahead brakes suddenly.
theory.followingDistance.2.ask: About a second passes before your foot is on the brake. How far do you drive in it?
theory.followingDistance.2.why: At 60 km/h you cover almost 17 m each second. The rule of thumb for this reaction distance: speed ÷ 10 × 3 – here 18 m.
theory.followingDistance.3.ask: How long is your stopping distance from 60 km/h – reacting and braking normally?
theory.followingDistance.3.why: Reaction distance 18 m plus braking distance (speed ÷ 10)² = 36 m: 54 m. In an emergency stop the braking part is about half as long. With 30 m to the car ahead you still stop in time.
theory.narrowPass.title: A cyclist, then an obstacle
theory.narrowPass.intro: A country road. A cyclist rides ahead of you; further on a lorry has broken down in your lane.
theory.narrowPass.1.text: The road ahead is clear. You overtake the cyclist.
theory.narrowPass.1.ask: Outside town: how much room must you leave beside the cyclist at least?
theory.narrowPass.1.why: Overtaking somebody on a bicycle, on foot or on an e-scooter, keep at least 2 m to the side outside town and at least 1.5 m in town.
theory.narrowPass.2.text: The lorry stands in your lane with its hazard lights on. A car comes towards you.
theory.narrowPass.2.why: Whoever has the obstacle on their side waits and lets the oncoming traffic through. Then pull out with room to spare – watching the traffic behind and indicating as you pull out and back in.
theory.busStopPullOut.title: A bus at its stop
theory.busStopPullOut.intro: In town. Ahead of you a bus stands at its stop and people get off.
theory.busStopPullOut.1.text: The bus has its hazard lights on while people get off.
theory.busStopPullOut.1.walk: Only at walking pace, with room enough
theory.busStopPullOut.1.why: While a bus stands at its stop with its hazard lights on, pass it only at walking pace and so far away that nobody is in danger – oncoming traffic too. Stop if you must.
theory.busStopPullOut.2.text: The bus switches to its left indicator: it wants to leave the stop.
theory.busStopPullOut.2.why: Line buses and school buses must be able to leave their marked stops – wait for them if you must.
theory.nightDrive.title: At night
theory.nightDrive.intro: A country road in the dark. You drive with full beam.
theory.nightDrive.1.ask: What do you do with your full beam?
theory.nightDrive.1.keep: Keep it on – I need to see
theory.nightDrive.1.why: Dip your headlights in good time when a vehicle comes towards you or drives close ahead – full beam dazzles. Switch it back on once the way is clear.
theory.nightDrive.2.text: With dipped headlights you see only some 50 to 60 m of the road.
theory.nightDrive.2.sight: Only so fast that I can stop within the distance I can see
theory.nightDrive.2.high: As fast as with full beam
theory.nightDrive.2.why: You must be able to stop within the distance you can see – at night, the reach of your lights. People in dark clothes at the edge of the road are seen even later.
theory.fogWall.title: Fog
theory.fogWall.intro: A country road. Ahead, the fog closes in.
theory.fogWall.1.text: You can hardly make out the next guide post – they stand 50 m apart. You see less than 50 m.
theory.fogWall.1.ask: How fast may you drive at most?
theory.fogWall.1.why: When fog, snow or rain leave you less than 50 m to see, drive no faster than 50 km/h – slower if need be.
theory.fogWall.2.fog: Dipped headlights and the rear fog light
theory.fogWall.2.why: Fog that hampers the view calls for dipped headlights by day too. The rear fog light only when you see less than 50 m – otherwise it dazzles those behind you. Full beam only lights up the fog.
theory.accidentScene.title: An accident ahead
theory.accidentScene.intro: A country road. Ahead of you two cars have crashed.
theory.accidentScene.1.text: Two cars stand crashed in the road ahead.
theory.accidentScene.1.hazard: Hazard lights on, stop well behind, put on the high-visibility vest
theory.accidentScene.1.help: Stop right by the cars and run to them
theory.accidentScene.1.why: Warn those behind with your hazard lights and stop well behind the accident. Put on the high-visibility vest and get out on the side away from the traffic – first make the place safe, then help.
theory.accidentScene.2.text: You have stopped behind the accident.
theory.accidentScene.2.ask: How far back do you put up the warning triangle on this country road?
theory.accidentScene.2.why: Where traffic is fast, about 100 m – so that those coming can slow down in time. In town about 50 m is usual, on the motorway further. Walk back along the edge, the triangle held in front of you.
theory.accidentScene.3.text: Somebody stands by the cars, hurt.
theory.accidentScene.3.all: Everybody who comes by – as far as they can
theory.accidentScene.3.involved: Only those involved in the accident
theory.accidentScene.3.why: Everybody must help as far as they can and may reasonably be asked to – failing to help is a criminal offence. Those involved must stop, make the place safe and look after the injured. Call 112.
theory.truckBlindSpot.title: The lorry turns right
theory.truckBlindSpot.intro: A red light. A lorry waits in front of you to turn right; a cycle lane runs beside it.
theory.truckBlindSpot.1.text: A cyclist rolls up beside the lorry – right in its blind spot (orange).
theory.truckBlindSpot.1.why: Turning traffic lets those going straight on along the cycle lane go first. From its high cab the cyclist is hard to see – on a bicycle, never stop beside a lorry's right side: wait behind it.
theory.truckBlindSpot.2.text: The cyclist has gone. The lorry turns.
theory.truckBlindSpot.2.ask: How fast may the lorry turn right here in town?
theory.truckBlindSpot.2.why: In town a lorry of more than 3.5 t turns right at walking pace wherever cyclists riding straight on or people crossing may be about – so that its driver can still stop.
theory.multiLane.title: Two lanes, then one
theory.multiLane.intro: Dense traffic in town, two lanes your way. The right lane ends ahead.
theory.multiLane.1.text: The blue car beside you indicates left: it wants into your lane now, though there is no room.
theory.multiLane.1.keep: Keep going steadily – it must wait for a safe gap
theory.multiLane.1.brake: Brake hard to let it in at once
theory.multiLane.1.why: Whoever changes lanes must make sure nobody is put in danger, and indicate in good time. Keep going steadily – braking hard could get you hit from behind. Taking turns applies right where a lane ends.
theory.multiLane.2.text: The right lane ends here. The blue car has driven on to its end.
theory.multiLane.2.why: Where a lane ends the cars take turns: one from the lane that goes on, one from the lane that ends – the zip. Let it in in front of you.
theory.tunnel.title: Through a tunnel
theory.tunnel.intro: A country road leads into a tunnel. It is daytime, your lights are off.
theory.tunnel.1.why: In a tunnel you drive with dipped headlights, however bright it is inside – and you never turn round in it.
theory.tunnel.2.text: Your engine fails in the tunnel. You roll to a stop at the right.
theory.tunnel.2.out: Hazard lights, engine off, key left in – out with the vest on, to the emergency telephone
theory.tunnel.2.stay: Stay in the car and wait for help
theory.tunnel.2.turn: Turn round and drive back out
theory.tunnel.2.why: Hazard lights on – in a tunnel use a breakdown bay or emergency lay-by if you can reach one, otherwise stop as far right as you can. Engine off, key left in for the rescuers. Get out with the high-visibility vest on, away from the traffic, and call for help from an emergency telephone; take an emergency exit if smoke comes.
theory.seniorCrossing.title: An old lady crosses
theory.seniorCrossing.intro: In town, no crossing nearby. An old lady with a rollator wants to cross the road.
theory.seniorCrossing.1.text: She steps off the kerb – slowly.
theory.seniorCrossing.1.brake: Slow down, ready to stop – and let her cross
theory.seniorCrossing.1.horn: Sound the horn so that she waits
theory.seniorCrossing.1.why: With children, old people and those who need help, slow down and be ready to brake – so that no danger to them can arise, even when they do something unexpected.
theory.seniorCrossing.2.text: She is past your half of the road but still on the carriageway.
theory.seniorCrossing.2.after: When she has reached the pavement
theory.seniorCrossing.2.why: She may stop, turn round or stumble. Wait until she is safely on the pavement – and do not hurry her.
theory.wildlife.title: Deer at dusk
theory.wildlife.intro: Dusk on a country road through a forest. The sign warns of deer crossing.
theory.wildlife.1.text: A deer stands at the edge of the forest ahead.
theory.wildlife.1.brake: Brake, dip the lights, sound the horn
theory.wildlife.1.flash: Full beam on to scare it away
theory.wildlife.1.why: Brake at once, dip the lights – full beam dazzles the animal and it freezes – and sound the horn. If you cannot avoid it, brake hard and keep straight: swerving into a tree or into the oncoming traffic is far worse.
theory.wildlife.2.text: The deer has crossed the road.
theory.wildlife.2.more: Not yet – more may follow; then on slowly
theory.wildlife.2.why: Deer and wild boar seldom come alone: where one has crossed, others follow. Wait a moment, then go on slowly and ready to brake – able to stop within the distance you can see.
theory.policeSignals.title: A police officer directs the traffic
theory.policeSignals.intro: The traffic lights work, but a police officer stands in the middle of the crossroads.
theory.policeSignals.1.text: Your light is green. The officer faces you, both arms out to the sides.
theory.policeSignals.1.why: A police officer's signs come before traffic lights, signs and all other rules. Facing you or with his back to you, arms out: stop. The traffic from the sides may go.
theory.policeSignals.2.ask: What does it mean for you?
theory.policeSignals.2.wait: Wait at the line for his next sign
theory.policeSignals.2.go: Go – a raised arm means the way is free
theory.policeSignals.2.why: One arm raised: wait for the next sign, as at amber. Whoever is already in the crossroads drives on and clears it.
theory.policeSignals.3.text: He turns his side to you and holds his arms out again.
theory.policeSignals.3.why: His side to you, arms out: the way is free for you – the traffic he faces must stop. Turning is allowed too, but turning left you still give way to oncoming traffic.
theory.flagman.title: A flagman at roadworks
theory.flagman.intro: A country road. Roadworks close your lane; a man with a stop/go sign lets the traffic through by turns.
theory.flagman.1.text: He shows you the red side of his sign.
theory.flagman.1.slow: Pass slowly on the other lane
theory.flagman.1.horn: Sound the horn and drive on
theory.flagman.1.why: Before roadworks begin, the road authority decides how the traffic past them is to be regulated – here by a worker with a stop/go sign. He is no police officer, but his red side means the one open lane belongs to the oncoming traffic: driving on would put you head-on with it. Stop and wait.
theory.flagman.2.text: The oncoming cars have passed. He turns his sign to green.
theory.flagman.2.slow: Slowly on the other lane, watching out for the workers
theory.flagman.2.fast: Quickly, so that the others need not wait long
theory.flagman.2.wait: I wait – more may come towards me
theory.flagman.2.why: Green means go – but slowly and carefully: people work right beside your way and the lane is narrow. Back into your lane after the roadworks, indicating.
lesson.truckNote: With truck and trailer: 60 km/h outside built-up areas, 80 km/h on the motorway.
lesson.capNote: {vehicle}: at most {rural} km/h outside built-up areas, {motorway} km/h on the motorway.
lesson.noMotorwayNote: With the tractor: at most 40 km/h, and never on the motorway.
lesson.slowNote: {vehicle}: at most {max} km/h, and never on the motorway.
lesson.ceCouple.title: CE 1 · Coupling and uncoupling
lesson.ceCouple.intro: Part of every test for class CE: uncouple the trailer and couple it again, in the right order. Secure the trailer before the lines come off; red comes off first and goes on last; couple in two steps. What is done on foot you choose from a list while the truck stands with the handbrake on.
lesson.ceCorner.title: CE 2 · Reversing round a corner to the left
lesson.ceCorner.intro: Reverse the combination from the road into the side road on the left. The trailer goes where the rear of the truck pushes it: steer little and early, and watch both mirrors. Pulling forward to correct is allowed twice. Done when truck and trailer stand straight in the side road with the handbrake on.
lesson.ceRamp.title: CE 3 · Reversing to the ramp, offset to the right
lesson.ceRamp.intro: Reverse to the loading ramp and move over to the right into the marked bay on the way. Stop at most a metre before the ramp without touching it, the trailer square to it. Pulling forward to correct is allowed twice.
lesson.bParallel.title: B · Parallel parking
lesson.bParallel.intro: Reverse into the gap between the two parked cars, parallel to the kerb and at most 30 cm from it, without touching the kerb or the cars. Two corrections are allowed. Done when the car stands straight in the gap with the handbrake on.
lesson.bBay.title: B · Bay parking forwards and backwards
lesson.bBay.intro: Park in the green bay between the parked cars: first forwards, then backwards. Stay within the lines, do not touch the cars or the kerb, and stand straight in the bay with the handbrake on. Two corrections are allowed each time.
lesson.bReverse.title: B · Reversing straight and round a corner
lesson.bReverse.intro: First, as practice, reverse straight along the marked lane into the green box without crossing the lines. Then reverse round the corner to the right into the side road, close to the kerb without touching it, and stand straight in the side road with the handbrake on.
lesson.bTurn.title: B · Turning round in a narrow street
lesson.bTurn.intro: Turn the car round in the narrow street – forwards, backwards, forwards – without touching the kerbs, and drive away on the right in the other direction. Two more moves are allowed as corrections.
lesson.bHill.title: B · Hill start on a ramp
lesson.bHill.intro: Practice for the test drive – the hill start is not one of the basic tasks of class B. Drive up the 10 % ramp and stop at the white line. Secure the car with the handbrake. Then pull away with the handbrake technique: first gear, clutch to the biting point, a little gas, release the handbrake – without rolling back more than 20 cm.
lesson.bBrake.title: B · Emergency stop
lesson.bBrake.intro: Drive along the lane at about 30 km/h. At the instructor’s signal brake as hard as you can – at once, with full force, keeping the car straight in its lane. Your reaction time and stopping distance are judged.
lesson.bDrills.title: B · Basic tasks as in the test
lesson.bDrills.intro: As in the practical test, three basic tasks: the examiner picks reversing round a corner or parallel parking, then two of turning round, bay parking and the emergency stop. A task that goes wrong may be repeated once.

drill.bayFwd.name: Bay parking forwards
drill.bayBack.name: Bay parking backwards

drill.step.pAlign: Drive up beside the car in front of the gap, about half a metre to a metre away, your rear level with its rear – and stop.
drill.step.pTurnIn: Reverse slowly with full lock to the right until the car stands at about 45° to the kerb.
drill.step.pBack: Wheels straight: reverse on until your rear is close to the kerb and your front has passed the car in front.
drill.step.pCounter: Full lock to the left: reverse until the car is straight – stop before the car behind.
drill.step.pFinish: Pull forward a little if needed, at most 30 cm from the kerb – then stop and apply the handbrake.
drill.step.bfApproach: Drive slowly along the aisle, keeping well left of the bays.
drill.step.bfTurn: When your mirror is level with the first line of the green bay: full lock to the right.
drill.step.bfIn: Straighten the wheels as the car points into the bay and drive in slowly.
drill.step.bfStop: Stop before the kerb, straight in the bay – then apply the handbrake.
drill.step.bbPast: Drive past the green bay until your rear is about a metre past its far line – and stop.
drill.step.bbTurn: Reverse slowly with full lock to the right, watching both mirrors and the cars beside the bay.
drill.step.bbIn: Straighten the wheels as the car points into the bay and reverse in slowly.
drill.step.bbStop: Stop before the kerb, straight in the bay – then apply the handbrake.
drill.step.bsGear: Engage reverse and look back over your shoulder.
drill.step.bsBack: Reverse slowly in the middle of the lane – small steering movements only.
drill.step.bsStop: Stop with the whole car in the green box – then apply the handbrake.
drill.step.bcPast: Drive past the side road on the right, close to the kerb, and stop about a car’s length past the corner.
drill.step.bcBack: Reverse straight and close to the kerb until your rear wheel reaches the start of the curve.
drill.step.bcTurn: Steer to the right and follow the curve of the kerb at the same distance.
drill.step.bcIn: Straighten up in the side road, close to the kerb – stop clear of the main road and apply the handbrake.
drill.step.tFwd: Look round, then full lock to the left and drive slowly to the far kerb – stop before touching it.
drill.step.tBack: Full lock to the right and reverse slowly to the other kerb – stop before touching it.
drill.step.tAway: Full lock to the left and drive away on the right in the other direction.
drill.step.hUp: Drive up the ramp and stop with your front at the white line.
drill.step.hSecure: Apply the handbrake and take your foot off the brake.
drill.step.hGo: First gear, clutch to the biting point, a little gas – release the handbrake and pull away without rolling back.
drill.step.brSpeed: Accelerate to about 30 km/h and keep the speed – wait for the signal.
drill.step.brStop: Brake! As hard as you can, until the car stands.
drill.r.line: You crossed the line – back into the lane.
drill.r.touch: Stop! You touched the parked car.
drill.r.tooMany: That was more than two corrections.
drill.r.notInGap: Not quite: the car is not wholly in the gap.
drill.r.crooked: Not quite: the car is not straight yet.
drill.r.kerbFar: Not quite: you are {d} cm from the kerb – at most 30, please.
drill.r.noseIn: Forwards into the bay, please – the front towards the kerb.
drill.r.backIn: Backwards into the bay, please – the rear towards the kerb.
drill.r.notInBay: Not quite: the car is not wholly within the lines of the bay.
drill.r.notInBox: Not quite: the whole car must stand in the green box.
drill.r.notInSide: Not quite: the whole car must be in the side road, clear of the main road.
drill.r.atLine: Good – now secure the car with the handbrake.
drill.r.pastLine: You are past the line – stop at it next time.
drill.r.rolledFar: The car rolled back a long way – that would have hit the car behind.
drill.r.secured: Secured. Now pull away with the handbrake technique.
drill.r.noHandbrake: You pulled away without securing the car with the handbrake first.
drill.r.braked: Stopped after {d} m – reaction time {t} s.
