v.drillKerbTouch.title: Touched the kerb
v.drillKerbTouch.why: Drive slowly and watch the kerb in the mirror – the wheels may come close to it, but not touch it.
v.drillKerbOver.title: Drove over the kerb
v.drillKerbOver.why: A wheel went up onto the kerb. Stop as soon as you feel the kerb, and correct instead.
v.drillKerbFar.title: Parked {d} cm from the kerb
v.drillKerbFar.why: A parked car stands parallel to the kerb and close to it – at most about 30 cm away.
v.drillTouch.title: Touched a parked car
v.drillTouch.why: Watch the corners of your car and the cars around it. Stop in good time and correct – touching another car ends the task.
v.drillCorrections.title: More than two corrections
v.drillCorrections.why: Two corrections – pulling forwards or backwards again – are allowed in a basic task.
v.drillLine.title: Crossed the line
v.drillLine.why: Stay within the marked lane: slow down and steer little and early.
v.drillRollback.title: Rolled back {d} cm
v.drillRollback.why: On a hill hold the car with the handbrake until the engine pulls: biting point, a little gas, then release the handbrake.
v.drillHillBrake.title: Hill start without the handbrake
v.drillHillBrake.why: Stop at the line, secure the car with the handbrake, and only then pull away with the handbrake technique.
v.drillStall.title: Engine stalled
v.drillStall.why: On a slope the engine needs a little more gas: bring the clutch slowly to the biting point and add gas before releasing the handbrake.
v.drillBrakeSpeed.title: Not about 30 km/h at the signal ({v} km/h)
v.drillBrakeSpeed.why: The emergency stop is done from about 30 km/h: reach that speed in good time and keep it.
v.drillBrakeLate.title: Braked late ({t} s)
v.drillBrakeLate.why: At the signal move your foot to the brake at once – every tenth of a second is almost a metre at 30 km/h.
v.drillBrakeSoft.title: Did not brake with full force
v.drillBrakeSoft.why: In an emergency stop the brake pedal goes down as hard as possible (with ABS: keep it there, and steer if needed).
v.drillBrakeLong.title: Stopping distance too long ({d} m)
v.drillBrakeLong.why: Brake at once and with full force: from 30 km/h the car stands after about 11 metres.
lesson.tramLine.title: Tram: five stops
lesson.tramLine.intro: Drive the tram to the next five stops. The pedals are power and brake ([[KeyW]] / [[KeyS]]), the handbrake is the emergency brake. Before a switch, indicate to take the branch. At each stop: stop at the mark, open the doors ([[KeyG]]), let everybody off and on, close the doors – then go on. Mind the speed in curves and the lights where the track crosses a junction.
lesson.busLine.title: A bus line: five stops
lesson.busLine.intro: Call at the next five bus stops on your way: stop with the front door at the pole, open the doors ([[KeyG]]), let the people off and on, close the doors, indicate left and pull out.
lesson.ceExam.title: Test drive, class CE
lesson.ceExam.intro: As in the practical test: coupling and uncoupling, the two basic manoeuvres, then a drive in traffic. With a trailer that means 60 km/h outside built-up areas, 80 km/h on the motorway, right turns in town at walking pace and wide turns. A dangerous fault or ten fault points fail the test.
v.speed.title: Too fast: {speed} where {limit} km/h is allowed
v.speed.why: The limit applies from the sign onwards. Without a sign: 50 km/h in built-up areas, 100 km/h outside.
v.speedWalk.title: Walking pace exceeded ({speed} km/h)
v.speedWalk.why: In a traffic-calmed area (sign 325.1) you must drive at walking pace; pedestrians may use the whole street.
v.redLight.title: Ran a red light
v.redLight.why: Red means: stop before the junction and wait at the stop line.
v.stopLine.title: Over the stop line on red
v.stopLine.why: The stop line (sign 294) orders you to stop here. Coming to rest beyond it puts you in the way of pedestrians and crossing traffic – brake earlier and more evenly.
v.amberLight.title: Entered on amber
v.amberLight.why: Amber orders you to wait for the next signal. Carry on only if you can no longer stop safely.
v.stopSign.title: Did not stop at the stop sign
v.stopSign.why: Sign 206: the vehicle must come to a complete stop at the line even if the road is clear, then give way.
v.prioritySign.title: Failed to give way
v.prioritySign.why: Sign 205 “give way”: traffic on the other road must neither be endangered nor substantially hindered.
v.rightBeforeLeft.title: Ignored “right before left”
v.rightBeforeLeft.why: At junctions without signs, whoever comes from the right has priority – typical in residential areas and 30 km/h zones.
v.priorityRoundabout.title: Failed to give way at the roundabout
v.priorityRoundabout.why: With signs 215 and 205, traffic on the roundabout has priority. Do not indicate when entering; indicate right when leaving.
v.priorityDriveway.title: Endangered others when pulling onto the road
v.priorityDriveway.why: Coming out of a property, car park, traffic-calmed area or farm track you must rule out any danger to others.
v.leftTurnOncoming.title: Did not let oncoming traffic pass when turning
v.leftTurnOncoming.why: Turning left you must let oncoming vehicles pass – also on a green light without an arrow.
v.cutOff.title: Cut in front of another vehicle
v.cutOff.why: When pulling out, merging or changing lanes nobody may be endangered: mirrors, shoulder check, indicator, wait for a gap.
v.zebra.title: Ignored a pedestrian at the zebra crossing
v.zebra.why: Anyone visibly wanting to cross has priority. Approach at moderate speed and wait if necessary.
v.zebraSpeed.title: Approached the pedestrian crossing too fast
v.zebraSpeed.why: Approach pedestrian crossings at moderate speed when someone might cross.
v.pedestrian.title: Endangered a pedestrian
v.pedestrian.why: Pedestrians are the most vulnerable road users. Endangering them fails any test.
v.tramCurve.title: Too fast in the curve: {speed} km/h where {limit} km/h is safe
v.tramCurve.why: A tram cannot steer away: too fast in a curve it can derail. Brake before the curve.
v.tramStopMissed.title: Drove past a stop
v.tramStopMissed.why: The tram stops at every stop of its line: people are waiting for it.
v.tramStopPlace.title: Opened the doors away from the stop
v.tramStopPlace.why: Stop with the front of the tram at the stop's mark, then open the doors: the passengers get off onto the platform.
v.tramDoorsMoving.title: Moved with the doors open
v.tramDoorsMoving.why: The doors are opened only when the tram stands, and closed before it moves – passengers could fall.
v.tramPantoLoad.title: Lowered the pantograph while pulling
v.tramPantoLoad.why: Lowered while the motors draw current, the pantograph draws an arc that burns the wire and its head: power off first, then lower it.
v.tramPantoWireEnd.title: Ran under the end of the wire with the pantograph up
v.tramPantoWireEnd.why: Where the wire ends the pantograph must already be down – it would catch on the end of the wire and tear it down.
v.tramDoorsEarly.title: Closed the doors while passengers were getting off and on ({n})
v.tramDoorsEarly.why: Wait until everybody is through the doors, then close them.
v.pedRed.title: Crossed against the red pedestrian light
v.pedRed.why: Red means wait, on foot too. Press the button and wait for green; if it turns red while you are on the road, go on to the other side.
v.pedRoad.title: Walked along the road instead of the pavement
v.pedRoad.why: Where there is a pavement, people on foot use it. Walk on the road only where there is none, and then facing the traffic.
v.pedCrossing.title: Crossed right beside a crossing
v.pedCrossing.why: A zebra crossing or a pedestrian light is only a few steps away: cross there.
v.pedForcedBrake.title: A vehicle had to brake hard for you
v.pedForcedBrake.why: Cross only when the road is clear: look left, right and left again – where there is no crossing, the vehicles go first.
v.pedHit.title: Hit by a vehicle
v.pedHit.why: Look both ways before you step onto the road, and cross only when nothing is coming – at the zebra crossing or on green, once the vehicles have stopped.
emTipBehind: Blue lights behind you – make way to the right, slow down and stop if need be.
emTipCorridor: Blue lights behind you – form the emergency corridor: the left lane moves to the left, all others to the right.
emTipJunction: Emergency vehicle at the junction ahead – wait before the line, even on green, until it has passed.
emTipOncoming: Emergency vehicle coming towards you – slow down and keep well to the right.
v.emergencyBlock.title: Did not make way for an emergency vehicle
v.emergencyBlock.why: Blue lights together with the siren order everybody to make way at once: slow down, move to the right, stop if need be – and let it pass.
v.emergencyCorridor.title: No emergency corridor in slow traffic
v.emergencyCorridor.why: Where the traffic slows to walking pace or stops on a road with two or more lanes in your direction, leave a corridor at once: the left lane moves to the left, all others to the right.
v.emergencyJunction.title: Drove into the junction in front of an emergency vehicle
v.emergencyJunction.why: With blue lights and siren an emergency vehicle may cross on red and against the right of way. Wait before the junction – even on green – until it has passed.
v.busStopMissed.title: Drove past a stop
v.busStopMissed.why: On a line the bus calls at every stop: slow down in good time and stop with the front door at the pole.
v.busStopPlace.title: Opened the doors away from the stop
v.busStopPlace.why: People get on and off only at the stop: stand with the front door at the pole, then open the doors.
v.busDoorsMoving.title: Drove off with the doors open
v.busDoorsMoving.why: Close the doors before you drive off – people still get on and off.
v.busDoorsEarly.title: Closed the doors while people were still getting on
v.busDoorsEarly.why: Wait until everybody is through the doors, then close them.
v.busPullOut.title: Pulled out of the stop without indicating
v.busPullOut.why: Before you pull away from the kerb, indicate left and look back; the others have to let a bus out of its stop.
v.classSpeed.title: Too fast for this vehicle: {speed} where {limit} km/h is allowed
v.classSpeed.why: Trucks, buses and vehicles with a trailer have lower limits than cars outside built-up areas and on the motorway – even where the signs allow more.
v.motorwayBan.title: Drove onto the motorway with a tractor
v.motorwayBan.why: Only vehicles built for more than 60 km/h may use the motorway.
v.doorCheck.title: Opened the door without looking back
v.doorCheck.why: Before getting out: mirror, then a look over the left shoulder – cyclists and cars pass close to the door.
v.doorTraffic.title: Opened the door in front of approaching traffic
v.doorTraffic.why: Whoever gets out must not endanger anybody: wait until nothing comes from behind, then open the door.
v.notSecured.title: Left the vehicle without securing it
v.notSecured.why: Before getting out: engine off and the parking brake on.
v.preCheck.title: Drove off without checking everything: {missing}
v.preCheck.why: Before driving off, walk round the vehicle: tyres, lights at the front and at the back – with a trailer the coupling.
v.cyclistCutOff.title: Cut off a cyclist while turning
v.cyclistCutOff.why: Cyclists who ride straight on beside you go first when you turn. Before turning right: mirror, shoulder check to the right – and wait until they have passed.
v.cyclistHit.title: Hit a cyclist
v.cyclistHit.why: Cyclists beside and behind the vehicle are hard to see, and nothing protects them. Look over your shoulder before you turn or move over. This fails any test.
v.noIndicator.title: Turned without indicating
v.noIndicator.why: Announce a turn clearly and in good time – keep the indicator on until the manoeuvre is finished.
v.wrongIndicator.title: Wrong indicator
v.wrongIndicator.why: The indicator must match where you actually go; a wrong signal misleads others.
v.indicatorLeftOn.title: Indicator left on
v.indicatorLeftOn.why: A forgotten indicator announces a turn that never happens.
v.noShoulderCheck.title: No shoulder check
v.noShoulderCheck.why: Check the traffic behind you once more before turning: cyclists in the blind spot can only be seen with a look over the shoulder.
v.roundaboutEntryIndicator.title: Indicated when entering the roundabout
v.roundaboutEntryIndicator.why: Do not indicate when entering a roundabout – only right when leaving.
v.roundaboutExitIndicator.title: Left the roundabout without indicating
v.roundaboutExitIndicator.why: Leaving a roundabout is a turn and must be indicated to the right.
v.turnBan.title: Took a prohibited direction
v.turnBan.why: Mandatory directions (blue arrow signs) and turn bans are binding.
v.wrongWay.title: Drove against the direction of traffic
v.wrongWay.why: Sign 267 forbids entry; one-way streets may only be used in the direction of the arrow.
v.keepRight.title: Not keeping to the right
v.keepRight.why: Keep as far right as possible – not only with oncoming traffic, when being overtaken, on crests or in bends.
v.sidewalk.title: Drove on the pavement
v.sidewalk.why: Vehicles must use the carriageway. The pavement belongs to pedestrians.
v.offRoad.title: Left the road
v.offRoad.why: Stay on the carriageway; verges and green areas are not lanes.
v.accessPrivate.title: No entry for vehicles
v.accessPrivate.why: Sign 250 prohibits all vehicles; private drives and company premises are off limits.
v.accessAgricultural.title: Used a farm track
v.accessAgricultural.why: Farm and forest tracks are usually open to agricultural and forestry traffic only (sign 260 with plate).
v.accessDestination.title: Residents and visitors only
v.accessDestination.why: “Anlieger frei” allows entry only if your destination is there.
v.distance.title: Following too closely ({gap} m)
v.distance.why: Rule of thumb outside towns: half the speedometer reading in metres. In town at least one second.
v.crash.title: Collision with another vehicle
v.crash.why: A collision ends every driving test. Look ahead and be ready to brake.
v.crashObject.title: Hit an obstacle ({speed} km/h)
v.crashObject.why: Choose speed and distance so that the vehicle is under control at all times.
v.stall.title: Engine stalled
v.stall.why: Let the clutch come up slowly to the biting point, add a little throttle, then release fully.
v.seatbelt.title: Seat belt not fastened
v.seatbelt.why: Prescribed seat belts must be worn while driving.
v.handbrakeOn.title: Driving with the handbrake on
v.handbrakeOn.why: Release the parking brake before driving off (watch the warning lamp).
v.ceLine.title: Crossed the boundary line
v.ceLine.why: The lines stand for kerbs and walls: neither the truck nor the trailer may cross them. Drive slower and watch both mirrors.
v.ceCorrections.title: More than two corrections
v.ceCorrections.why: Pulling forward to straighten the combination is allowed twice in each task.
v.ceRamp.title: Hit the ramp
v.ceRamp.why: Stop before the ramp: at most a metre away, never touching it. Reverse at walking pace and stop early.
v.ceSecure.title: Lines taken off before the trailer was secured
v.ceSecure.why: First secure the trailer – parking brake, wheel chocks, support leg – and only then take off lines and cables.
v.ceAir.title: Air lines in the wrong order
v.ceAir.why: Uncoupling: red (supply) first, then yellow (brake). Coupling: yellow first, then red. Red is never connected alone – the trailer’s brakes would release.
v.ceOpen.title: Coupling opened with lines still connected
v.ceOpen.why: All lines and cables come off before the coupling is opened – they would tear when the truck pulls away.
v.ceLocked.title: Carried on without checking the coupling
v.ceLocked.why: After coupling, first check that the coupling is closed and locked. Only then connect the lines and raise the support leg.
v.ceRelease.title: Trailer released before its brakes had air
v.ceRelease.why: Wheel chocks and the trailer’s parking brake are released only when both air lines are connected.
v.ceLights.title: Lights checked without the cable
v.ceLights.why: Connect the electrical cable first, then check the trailer’s lights.
v.ceHeight.title: Coupled without stopping to look
v.ceHeight.why: Coupling is done in two steps: stop about a metre before the drawbar eye, get out, compare heights and alignment – then reverse the last metre.
v.ceFast.title: Bumped into the trailer
v.ceFast.why: The last metre is driven at a crawl. A hard knock damages coupling and drawbar and can push the trailer away.
v.truckRightTurn.title: Turned right faster than walking pace ({speed} km/h)
v.truckRightTurn.why: In built-up areas trucks turn right at walking pace: cyclists and pedestrians beside the truck are hard to see.
v.truckSpeed.title: Too fast with a trailer: {speed} where {limit} km/h is allowed
v.truckSpeed.why: With a trailer a truck may drive 60 km/h outside built-up areas and 80 km/h on the motorway – even where signs allow others more.
